_comment: Maps the FEC's free-text `pur` (purpose) field on a Schedule E row to a
medium. This lives in a data file rather than inline regexes because it is
an editorial judgement about what a filer meant, and it will be argued
with: filers write whatever they like, and 93 distinct purpose strings
THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: much of Schedule E is not advertising at
all. 'IE- CRUZ - DONATION PROCESSING', 'BANK CHARGES AND FEES' and
'STAFF TIME - IE DEBT PAYMENT' are overhead; 'CANVASSING' and
'PHONEBANKING' are field organising. Folding those into an advertising
total would overstate how much was spent on the messages a voter saw,
which is the entire question this dataset exists to answer. `is_ad`
marks the buckets that represent a placed message.
'MEDIA PLACEMENT' with no medium named is genuinely ambiguous — it is
commonly TV but not reliably so — and goes to media_unspecified rather
than being guessed into tv. Anything unmatched stays `unclassified` and
notes: Matching is substring, case-insensitive, first bucket in declaration
order wins. Order therefore matters: 'digital advertising' must hit
digital before the broader 'advertising' in media_unspecified, so
Buckets with is_ad=false must never be summed into an 'advertising
